# I2C on Senseair Sunrise and Sunlight

Notes from `TDE5531.pdf` (document `TDE5531`, rev. `18`, 56 pages, revision history dated 2025-10-21).

## Scope

This is the `I2C` protocol and register reference for Senseair Sunrise and Sunlight. It is the authoritative source for host-side `I2C` behavior, register addresses, EEPROM-backed configuration, and the state that must be preserved in single-measurement mode when the sensor is powered down between measurements.

## Electrical and protocol basics

- Sensor role: `I2C` target only; it never initiates communication.
- Addressing mode: `7-bit`.
- Default address: `0x68`.
- Supported rate: up to `100 kbit/s` (standard mode).
- Clock stretching: supported. For `006-0-0002` and `006-0-0007`, the EEPROM and RAM write times below are the intervals during which the sensor may hold `SCL` low.
- `SCL` has an internal `100 kOhm` pull-up.
- `SDA` has no internal pull-up; add an external pull-up.
- The vendor recommends external pull-ups in the `5 kOhm` to `15 kOhm` range on both `SCL` and `SDA` in most designs.

## Wake-up behavior

The sensor spends most of its time in deep sleep and wakes on a falling edge on `SDA`, so `I2C` access is a two-step process:

1. Wake it by sending its address with `START ... address ... STOP`.
2. Begin normal `I2C` communication within `15 ms`.

Important details:

- When the sensor is asleep, the wake-up address byte is not acknowledged.
- If the sensor was already awake (for example during a measurement), the address is acknowledged.
- Every byte sent to or from the sensor refreshes the `15 ms` timeout.
- After a complete read or write transaction, the sensor immediately returns to sleep.

## Write timing

- RAM write time: `<1 ms`.
- EEPROM write time:
  - `006-0-0002` and `006-0-0007`: `<25 ms`
  - other articles: `<107 ms`

The document explicitly warns not to power the sensor down while EEPROM writes are in progress, because parameters can be corrupted.

## Core read-only registers

## ErrorStatus

`ErrorStatus` is split across `0x00` (MSB) and `0x01` (LSB).

### MSB bits

| Bit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Low internal regulated voltage |
| 1 | Measurement timeout |
| 2 | Abnormal signal level (not applicable for `006-0-0007`) |
| 7 | Scale factor error (firmware `4.10+`) |

Bits `3-6` are reserved.

Article-specific behavior:

- Bit `0`, general: set if the internal regulated voltage dropped below `2.8 V` and the sensor reset; cleared by a power-off/on, a reset command, or a write to `Clear ErrorStatus`.
- Bit `0`, `006-0-0007`: set while supply voltage is below `2.8 V`; cleared automatically when the internal voltage normalizes.
- Bit `1`: set together with the self-diagnostics flag, except on `006-0-0007`, where it can be set independently.

### LSB bits

| Bit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Fatal error |
| 1 | `I2C` error / invalid access |
| 2 | Algorithm error / corrupt parameters |
| 3 | Calibration error |
| 4 | Self-diagnostics error |
| 5 | Out of range |
| 6 | Memory error |
| 7 | No measurement completed |

Bit `7` is set at sensor startup and cleared after the **first** measurement. The document describes it as a completion check for single-measurement mode when the sensor is powered down between measurements. It is not a per-measurement flag: if the sensor stays powered, it remains clear after the first measurement. Use `nRDY` or the measurement count (`0x0D`) to detect later measurements.

## Measurement and identity registers

| Register(s) | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0x06-0x07` | Filtered, pressure-compensated measured concentration, signed `16-bit`, ppm |
| `0x08-0x09` | Chip temperature, signed `16-bit`, unit `0.01 C` |
| `0x0D` | Measurement count, `0-255`, increments after each measurement and wraps |
| `0x0E-0x0F` | Measurement cycle time, increments every `2 s` within the current cycle; reset to `0` at the start of each measurement |
| `0x10-0x11` | Unfiltered, pressure-compensated concentration |
| `0x12-0x13` | Filtered concentration |
| `0x14-0x15` | Unfiltered concentration |
| `0x1A-0x1B` | Scaled measured concentration (`4.10+`) |
| `0x2A-0x2D` | Elapsed time counter (ETC), unsigned `32-bit`, hours the sensor has been powered up (`4.10+`) |
| `0x2F` | Firmware type |
| `0x38-0x39` | Firmware revision (main, sub) |
| `0x3A-0x3D` | Sensor ID, unsigned `32-bit` |
| `0x70-0x7F` | Product code in ASCII, null-terminated (firmware `4.08+`) |

The ETC counts only while the sensor is powered, so it cannot measure time spent shut down.

### Register-selection guidance

- Use `0x12-0x13` when you want filtered but not pressure-compensated `CO2`.
- Use `0x06-0x07` when you want the filtered value after pressure compensation.
- Use `0x14-0x15` or `0x10-0x11` when you need unfiltered values.
- With pressure compensation disabled (the default), `0x06-0x07` equals `0x12-0x13` and `0x10-0x11` equals `0x14-0x15`.
- `0x0D` and `0x0E-0x0F` are useful for host synchronization.

## Core writable registers

## Calibration-related registers

| Register(s) | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0x81` | Calibration status |
| `0x82-0x83` | Calibration command |
| `0x84-0x85` | Calibration target for target calibration |
| `0x86-0x87` | Measured concentration override; default `32767` (no override); writing a lower value forces both filtered and unfiltered concentration to that value after the next measurement |

Calibration commands:

| Command | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0x7C02` | Restore factory calibration |
| `0x7C03` | Forced ABC calibration (only works if ABC is enabled and the sensor has valid ABC data) |
| `0x7C05` | Target calibration |
| `0x7C06` | Background calibration (uses the ABC target) |
| `0x7C07` | Zero calibration |

The sensor calibrates on the **first measurement after** it receives the command. In single-measurement mode, the host must trigger a measurement after writing the command. All later measurements use the adjusted calibration.

The document recommends clearing `CalibrationStatus` before starting a calibration.

CalibrationStatus success bits:

| Bit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 2 | Factory calibration restored |
| 3 | ABC calibration |
| 4 | Target calibration |
| 5 | Background calibration |
| 6 | Zero calibration |

## Measurement-mode and timing configuration

| Register(s) | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0x93` | Start single measurement |
| `0x95` | Measurement mode (`0 = continuous`, `1 = single`) (EE) |
| `0x96-0x97` | Continuous-mode measurement period in seconds; range `2-65534`; odd values rounded up to nearest even (EE) |
| `0x98-0x99` | Number of samples; range `1-1024` (EE) |

Important notes:

- Changing `0x95`, `0x96-0x97`, or `0x98-0x99` requires a sensor reset before the new values take effect or can be read back.
- Default measurement period is `16 s`; it is only used in continuous mode.
- Default number of samples is `8`.
- One sample takes at most `300 ms`, so `number_of_samples * 0.3 s` should be less than or equal to the time between measurements. If the samples take longer than the period, the actual period is extended.
- Except on `006-0-0007`, odd sample counts are rounded down to the nearest even number, and values below `2` become `2`.

## ABC, filter, and meter control

| Register(s) | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0x88-0x89` | ABC time: hours since the last ABC calibration |
| `0x8A-0x91` | ABC parameters (`ABC Par0-Par3`) |
| `0x9A-0x9B` | ABC period in hours, range `1-65534`, default `180` (EE) |
| `0x9D` | Clear ErrorStatus (write any value) |
| `0x9E-0x9F` | ABC target in ppm; also the background-calibration target (EE) |
| `0xA1` | Static IIR filter parameter (`2-10`; higher means stronger filtering) (EE) |
| `0xA3` | `SCR` software reset (`0xFF` resets sensor) |
| `0xA5` | Meter control bitfield (EE) |

ABC is enabled when the ABC period is `1-65534` and meter-control bit `1` is `0`. Writing `0` or `65535` to the ABC period, or setting bit `1`, disables ABC.

### Meter control (`0xA5`)

| Bit | `0` means | `1` means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `nRDY` enabled (default) | `nRDY` disabled |
| 1 | ABC enabled (default) | ABC disabled |
| 2 | Static IIR enabled (default) | Static IIR disabled |
| 3 | Dynamic IIR enabled (default) | Dynamic IIR disabled |
| 4 | Pressure compensation enabled | Pressure compensation disabled (default) |
| 5 | `nRDY` invert enabled, low during measurement | `nRDY` invert disabled (default), high during measurement |

Important coupling:

- Dynamic IIR only works when static IIR is also enabled.
- Pressure compensation is disabled by default.

## Addressing and scaling

| Register(s) | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0xA7` | Modbus / `I2C` address (EE) |
| `0xA8-0xA9` | Concentration scale-factor numerator, unsigned `16-bit` (`4.10+`) (EE) |
| `0xAA-0xAB` | Concentration scale-factor denominator, unsigned `16-bit` (`4.10+`) (EE) |
| `0xAC-0xAD` | Scaled calibration target (`4.10+`) |
| `0xAE-0xAF` | Scaled measured concentration override (`4.10+`) |
| `0xB0-0xB1` | Scaled ABC target (`4.10+`) (EE) |

Address notes:

- Default address is `0x68`.
- Valid range is `0x01-0x7F`.
- A reset is required after changing the address.
- The sensor does not validate that the address is a sensible one; avoid reserved addresses.

Scaling notes:

- Scaled concentration = filtered pressure-compensated concentration `* numerator / denominator`.
- If numerator and denominator are both `0xFFFF`, scaling is disabled and the scaled register is a copy of `0x06-0x07`.
- Invalid scaling factors trigger the scale-factor error bit in `ErrorStatus` at startup.
- A reset is required to activate and read back new scaling values.

## State that must be preserved in single-measurement mode

This is the most important part of the document for low-power firmware.

When the sensor is powered down or `EN` is driven low between measurements, volatile state is lost. The host must read the state registers after each measurement and write them back after the next power-on, before triggering a measurement.

### State register block

Registers `0xC0-0xCD` mirror `0x80`, `0x81`, `0x92`, `0x93` and `0x88-0x91`. Registers `0xCE-0xDF` exist only at these addresses; they are not mirrors. Together they let the host read and write the state as one contiguous block.

| Register(s) | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0xC1` | Calibration status (mirror of `0x81`) |
| `0xC3` | Start single measurement (mirror of `0x93`) |
| `0xC4-0xC5` | ABC time (mirror of `0x88-0x89`) |
| `0xC6-0xCD` | ABC parameters (mirror of `0x8A-0x91`) |
| `0xCE-0xDB` | IIR filter parameters (`Filter Par0-Par6`) |
| `0xDC-0xDD` | Barometric pressure value, signed `16-bit`, unit `0.1 hPa`, valid range `3000-13000` |
| `0xDE-0xDF` | ABC barometric pressure value |

What must be preserved, and when:

- **ABC time and ABC parameters** (`0xC4-0xCD`), if ABC is enabled. The host must **increment ABC time by one for every hour that passes** while the sensor is powered down, then write it back.
- **Filter parameters** (`0xCE-0xDB`), if the IIR filter is enabled.
- **ABC barometric pressure** (`0xDE-0xDF`), if pressure compensation and ABC are both enabled.
- **Barometric pressure** (`0xDC-0xDD`) is an input, not saved state: write the current value each cycle when pressure compensation is enabled.

### Host sequence when state exists

The document's sequence (Figure 10) is:

1. Drive `EN` high (`>1.2 V`).
2. Wait at least `35 ms` for start-up and stabilization.
3. Write `Start Single Measurement` plus the saved state (`0xC3-0xDB`), or `0xC3-0xDD` to include pressure when pressure compensation is used, or `0xC3-0xDF` to also restore the ABC barometric pressure when pressure compensation and ABC are both enabled.
4. Wait for a falling edge on `nRDY` (with the default, non-inverted setting), or `2.4 s` with the default configuration.
5. Read the measurement: eight bytes from `0x00` (`ErrorStatus` first, measured concentration last).
6. Read the state (`0xC4-0xDB`, or `0xC4-0xDF` when pressure compensation and ABC are both enabled) and save it in host retention memory.
7. Drive `EN` low (`<0.4 V`).
8. Wait until the next measurement.

The `0xC3-0xDF` / `0xC4-0xDF` ranges follow from the register table (page 25), which requires `0xDE-0xDF` to be preserved when pressure compensation and ABC are both enabled; the vendor's worked example (pages 33 and 35) leaves them out.

Important ordering: if the start measurement command and state data are written in two separate `I2C` write sequences, the state data must be written before the start measurement command.

### Host sequence when state does not exist yet

The document is explicit here:

- Do not write zeroes or arbitrary values into `0xC6-0xDB` on the first cycle.
- Either (a) write only the start measurement command (`0xC3 = 0x01`); if pressure compensation is enabled, write pressure to `0xDC-0xDD` before the start command; or (b) skip the measurement and go straight to step 6 to read and save the sensor's initial state.

## Pressure compensation

Pressure-compensation write path:

- Enable compensation by clearing bit `4` in `MeterControl`.
- Write pressure in `0.1 hPa` to `0xDC-0xDD`.
- Valid range is `3000-13000`, corresponding to `300-1300 hPa`.
- If the value is outside range, the sensor uses `3000` or `13000` and sets `Out of range`.
- The new pressure is used in the next gas calculation; in continuous mode this can take up to one measurement period.

Example in the document:

- `997 hPa` becomes `9970`, which is `0x26F2`.

## EEPROM-backed registers

Registers marked `(EE)` are EEPROM-backed. The document repeats several cautions:

- total EEPROM writes should stay below `10000`,
- several `(EE)` writes in a single sequence count as one write cycle,
- on `006-0-0002` and `006-0-0007`, the sensor does not respond during EEPROM writes; writing several `(EE)` registers in one sequence can make it unresponsive for up to `100 ms`,
- communication responsiveness is not a reliable way to detect write completion,
- never power down the sensor during EEPROM writes.

Registers marked reserved can be read and written, but the document strongly recommends not using them.

## Examples that matter in practice

## Reading status and gas concentration

The example read transaction reads:

- `ErrorStatus`,
- four reserved bytes,
- measured concentration.

The example results `0x020C` and `0x01F2` correspond to `524 ppm` and `498 ppm`.

## Switching to single mode

To enter single-measurement mode:

1. write `0x01` to `0x95`,
2. reset the sensor.

## Triggering a single measurement

Write `0x01` to `0x93` or `0xC3`. If ABC is enabled, make sure the sensor periodically measures in fresh air (see the ABC section of `TDE7318`).

## Enabling and disabling ABC

- To enable ABC, set its period to `1-65534` and clear bit `1` in `MeterControl`.
- ABC disabled means set bit `1` in `MeterControl`.
- ABC period is configured through `0x9A-0x9B`; default is `180 hours`.
- Setting the ABC period to `0` also disables ABC, but the host must then remember the period to re-enable it.

## Enabling and disabling filtering

- Enable dynamic IIR by clearing bits `2` and `3`.
- Disable both static and dynamic IIR by setting bits `2` and `3`.

## Background calibration

Background calibration calibrates against the `ABC Target` (for `CO2`: fresh air or `400 ppm`). The continuous-mode example sequence is:

1. clear `CalibrationStatus` (`0x81 = 0x00`),
2. write command `0x7C06` to `0x82-0x83`,
3. read back `CalibrationStatus`.

Success example: `CalibrationStatus = 0x20`. The sensor should be in a stable environment.

In single-measurement mode (flowchart in section 3.7.1.2):

1. drive `EN` high and wait at least `35 ms`,
2. clear `CalibrationStatus` (recommended),
3. write the calibration command,
4. write the start measurement command plus saved state (only the start command if there is no state),
5. wait for `nRDY` to fall, or the sampling time (`2.4 s` for the default `8` samples),
6. read `CalibrationStatus`,
7. read and save the state, then drive `EN` low.

## Target calibration

The example target is `500 ppm`:

1. clear `CalibrationStatus`,
2. write `500` (`0x01F4`) to `0x84-0x85`,
3. write `0x7C05` to `0x82-0x83`,
4. read back status.

Success example: `CalibrationStatus = 0x10`.

## Changing the `I2C` address

The document's example sets the address to `10`:

1. write `0x0A` to `0xA7`,
2. reset the sensor with `0xA3 = 0xFF` (or power-cycle it),
3. communicate using address `0x0A`.

## Scaling-factor example

For firmware `4.10+`, the document shows changing the scaled concentration output for Sunlight `R32` to `%LFL` for `R454B`:

- numerator `0xA8-0xA9 = 4170 = 0x104A`
- denominator `0xAA-0xAB = 4096 = 0x1000`

Reset the sensor, then read both registers back to confirm.

## Gas scaling factors table from the document

The final section gives conversion constants for common sensor variants:

- `ppm = sensor reading * Kppm`
- `%LFL = sensor reading / K%LFL * 100%`

The document says these are theoretically calculated, product-dependent values: check the product specification and verify settings and readings in the real application.

| Gas | `Kppm` | `K%LFL` | Numerator | Denominator | `%LFL` LSB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `R32` | `10.00` | `144.4` | `22688` | `32768` | `0.01%` |
| `R454A` | `18.47` | `45.8` | `8948` | `4096` | `0.01%` |
| `R454B` | `12.06` | `98.2` | `4170` | `4096` | `0.01%` |
| `R454C` | `26.65` | `29.6` | `6910` | `2048` | `0.01%` |
| `R455A` | `27.67` | `43.6` | `18791` | `8192` | `0.01%` |
| `R290` | `1.00` | `210.0` | `100` | `210` | `0.01%` |

## Inconsistencies in the vendor document

These are errors in rev 18 itself; this file uses the values noted.

- Scaled measured concentration is at `0x1A-0x1B` (register table, page 15, and the section 3.11 example). Pages 22 and 53 refer to it as `0x18-0x19`.
- The ABC period description (page 21) refers to "addr `0xA4`, `0xA5`" for meter control; `0xA4` is reserved and meter control is `0xA5`.
- In the scaling example, the text and the write diagram (page 51) use `0x104A`. The readback diagram (page 52) still shows `0x4B`, with an "A" correction above it.

## What matters most for implementation

For firmware and driver work, the critical rules from this document are:

- always perform the wake-up byte before a sleeping sensor transaction,
- start the real transaction within `15 ms`,
- distinguish EEPROM-backed registers from RAM-backed ones,
- reset after changing mode, timing, address, or scaling settings that require activation,
- preserve ABC state, filter state, and ABC pressure state when powering the sensor down between single measurements, and advance ABC time by the hours spent powered down,
- do not fabricate state data on the first single-measurement cycle,
- trigger a measurement after a calibration command in single-measurement mode,
- do not rely on `ErrorStatus` bit `7` for completion unless the sensor was powered up for this measurement,
- use the right concentration register for filtered/unfiltered and pressure-compensated/non-compensated behavior.
